question: A bank pays compound interest at the rate of 5% per annum compounded half-yearly. A customer deposited Rs.1,600 each on 1st January and 1st July in a year. The interest he gets on the amount deposited at the end of the year is:
solution:
Given:

The bank offers compound interest at a rate of 5% per annum, compounded half-yearly.

The customer deposits Rs.1600 each on 1st January and 1st July of a year.

Concept:

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the rate is divided by 2 and the time is multiplied by 2.

Solution:

⇒ The interest for the first deposit for one year = P(1 + r/200)²t - P = 1600(1 + 5/200)² - 1600 = ₹ 81

⇒ The interest for the second deposit for six months = P(1 + r/200)t - P = 1600(1 + 5/200) - 1600 = ₹ 40.

⇒ Total interest = ₹ 81 + ₹ 40 = ₹ 121.

Therefore, at the end of the year, the customer will receive ₹ 121 as interest.
